theory.intro: Invert the ordinates of a graph to sketch its reciprocal.
facts: Zeros approached continuously give vertical asymptotes. Keep the original domain exclusions.
The sign stays the same. Points with $y=\pm1$ stay fixed.
Non-zero maxima become minima, and minima become maxima.
As $f(x)\to\pm\infty$, $1/f(x)\to0$. A non-zero horizontal limit $c$ becomes $1/c$.

workedExamples.question_text: By sketching each base function and reciprocating, sketch (a) $y=\frac1{(x+2)^2}$ and (b) $y=\frac1{(x+2)^3}$. Label the asymptotes and invariant points.
Let $f(x)=\frac{x-2}{x+2}$, with domain $\mathbb R\setminus\{-2\}$. Find the equation and domain of $g(x)=1/f(x)$, then sketch $g$, marking any excluded point and its asymptotes.
